audio.transcript_summary: English narration describes the magnitude 9.0 earthquake that shook northern Japan on March 11, 2011, centered about 80 miles offshore, triggering immediate tsunami warnings and causing residents of coastal cities to run to higher ground on hills and tall buildings where footage was captured. It describes people in Kesennuma watching from a high-rise rooftop as the tsunami inundated the city, and shows water overtopping an 18-foot seawall in Kamaishi City, described as the world's deepest and largest seawall, which was insufficient for the disaster. The narrator states this was the largest quake ever known in Japan and one of the five largest ever recorded in the world, with more than 28,000 confirmed dead or missing, caused by two tectonic plates pushing together under the sea.

final_verdict.summary: [Claim inferred from the post's title/caption (you did not enter one); date basis: spoken_in_narration.] The input URL was itself published on 2011-06-13 (per yt-dlp metadata), which is not before the claimed event date, so recycling relative to the claim is not established. The claim could not be verified from the available evidence. Media nature (AI observation from frames 7,13,20,27,34,40, not proof; does not change the label): Edited news report containing third-party clips — earlier copies of individual clips are expected and do not by themselves mean recycling.
limits: A visual match proves shared footage ('previously published'), not that a claim is false or that the footage is fake.
Upload dates are platform metadata (or an archive snapshot date, an upper bound) for the copy found; the earliest copy found is not necessarily the original source.
Search is not exhaustive: memory covers only indexed clips, reverse search rarely finds originals, and heavy crops/edits can evade hash shortlisting.
'Not found' means not found by these adapters, not that no earlier copy exists.
Dates are UTC calendar dates from the platform. Without an exact timestamp a copy must be dated at least 2 days before the claimed date to count as earlier (time-zone margin: Nepal is UTC+5:45).
